text:
We study the special algebraic properties of alternating 3-forms in 6 and 7 dimensions and introduce a diffeomorphism-invariant functional on the space of differential 3-forms on a closed manifold M in these dimensions. Restricting the functional to closed forms in a fixed cohomology class, we find that a critical point which is generic in a suitable sense defines in the 6-dimensional case a complex threefold with trivial canonical bundle and in 7 dimensions a Riemannian manifold with holonomy G2. This approach gives a direct method of finding a local moduli space, with its special geometry, for these structures.

1 Introduction This paper arose from the author’s interest in the geometry of 3 3 -forms on a manifold. Exterior differential forms of degree 2 2 are much studied, in particular a symplectic manifold is defined by a closed non-degenerate 2 2 -form. Our starting point here is the fact that in dimensions 6 6 and 7 7 the notion of non-degeneracy for three-forms makes sense too. By this we mean that if W W is a real vector space of dimension 6 6 or 7 7 , then the group G ​ L ​ ( W ) GL(W) has an open orbit, a fact that has been known for nearly a century [ 12 ] . The orbits we are particularly interested in have stabilizer conjugate to S ​ L ​ ( 3 , 𝐂 ) SL(3,\mathbf{C}) when dim W = 6 \dim W=6 , and the exceptional Lie group G 2 G_{2} when dim W = 7 \dim W=7 . In this way a single 3 3 -form Ω \Omega on a manifold M M defines a reduction of the structure group of M M to one of these groups. When we look closely at the mechanism for this reduction, there appears naturally a volume form algebraically defined by any 3 3 -form. Integrating this form gives a diffeomorphism-invariant functional Φ \Phi on the space of 3 3 -forms, and this is our main object of study. Following the analogy with Hodge theory, we restrict this functional to closed forms on M M in a given de Rham cohomology class and look for critical points. What we find is that if the critical point Ω \Omega is a 3 3 -form which lies in the open orbit everywhere, then the reduction of structure group is integrable in the sense that for dim M = 6 \dim M=6 we obtain a complex threefold with trivial canonical bundle, and for dim M = 7 \dim M=7 a Riemannian manifold with holonomy in G 2 G_{2} . These geometrical structures are therefore simply critical points of the invariant functionals. Because the functional is diffeomorphism-invariant, every critical point lies on an orbit of critical points and so Φ \Phi is never a Morse function. However, we show that formally it is a Morse-Bott function – its Hessian is non-degenerate transverse to the orbits of Diff ( M ) \mathop{\rm Diff}\nolimits(M) . In the 6 6 -dimensional case this requires the assumption that the complex threefold satisfies the ∂ ∂ ¯ \partial\bar{\partial} -lemma, and in the G 2 G_{2} case we need an analogue of this lemma, which is essentially contained in [ 7 ] . This nondegeneracy can be used, together with a standard use of the Banach space implicit function theorem, to give a direct and easy proof that the moduli space of complex structures together with holomorphic 3 3 -forms on a 6 6 -manifold is locally an open set in H 3 ​ ( M , 𝐑 ) H^{3}(M,\mathbf{R}) . In particular we see that the moduli space of complex structures is unobstructed. The novelty of our approach is that the flat structure on this moduli space is apparent from the very beginning, and the complex structure is defined in a secondary manner. This is the opposite point of view from the conventional use of Kodaira-Spencer theory as in the work of Tian and Todorov [ 14 ] , [ 15 ] . For us the complex structure on the moduli space carries with it the natural special pseudo-Kähler structure whose existence is an important ingredient in mirror symmetry [ 2 ] . We carry out the same process for G 2 G_{2} -manifolds and show that the moduli space is isomorphic to an open set in H 3 ​ ( M , 𝐑 ) H^{3}(M,\mathbf{R}) with an indefinite metric of Hessian type, completing a line of thought due to Joyce [ 7 ] . The structure of the paper is as follows. In Section 2 we consider the linear algebra of the vector space Λ 3 ​ W ∗ \Lambda^{3}W^{*} where W W is 6 6 -dimensional. The essential point is that over the complex numbers, a generic 3 3 -form is the sum of two decomposable ones. In Section 3, we see this algebra from the point of view of symplectic geometry, regarding Λ 3 ​ W ∗ \Lambda^{3}W^{*} as a symplectic vector space under the action of S ​ L ​ ( W ) SL(W) . This viewpoint is extremely useful for studying the variational problem. Section 4 is a detour into the realm of self-duality. With an inner product of signature ( 5 , 1 ) (5,1) on W W , we can define self-dual and anti-self-dual 3 3 -forms, and some of the linear algebra assumes a much more concrete form. Moreover, we see a setting here for the equation of motion for a self-interacting self-dual tensor, a nonlinear equation of some current interest to physicists. In Section 5 we introduce the invariant functional on 3 3 -forms on a 6 6 -manifold, and relate the critical points to integrable complex structures. In Section 6 we prove Morse-Bott nondegeneracy formally, and then use a Sobolev space model to prove rigorously that an open set in H 3 ​ ( M , 𝐑 ) H^{3}(M,\mathbf{R}) is a local moduli space. Section 7 is concerned with carrying out the parallel programme for G 2 G_{2} -manifolds. The author wishes to thank Robert Bryant for explaining the algebra behind S ​ L ​ ( 3 , 𝐂 ) SL(3,\mathbf{C}) and G 2 G_{2} and Patrick Baier for useful discussions.
